The Arcade · The DroverThe Sluice-Gate

You cannot push a flock — but you can slide a gate. Two sluice paddles ride the channel walls; drag one down and its flat edge sweeps the herd ahead of it, through the opening and on. Time two sweeps and the whole flock threads the S into the fold. No clock, no score — just the water-quiet of getting the timing right.

↳ the Drover's third star — kin to The Shepherd (there you chose where to stand) and The Standing Stones (there you set fixed repellers and released). Here the walls themselves move: you choose when to open the gate. One verified flock law, three verbs.

Grab a gate's handle and drag it down the wall — or hold A/D for gate 1, ↓/↑ for gate 2. The flock is swept ahead of the flat edge; nothing else moves it.
The quiet correctness layer self-test: …
No overlap, ever — under motion.EXACT min pairwise sheep-separation stays > 0 at every step even when a gate is slammed into the pack. A positional barrier the moving wall cannot outrun. —
WIN ≡ allInFold.EXACT The fold latches iff every sheep is inside the concave cove — no timer race — and live play is replayable byte-identical from the recorded gate trace. —
Neg-control.EXACT The funnel with the gates frozen open never folds the flock — the SWEEP is load-bearing. Press Jam the gates and feel it. —
MODELED The flock runs a believable herding model — Reynolds boids (separation / alignment / cohesion) with a tiny wander, the same law The Shepherd and The Standing Stones are built on, ridden here UNFORKED. A moving gate is just a re-supplied wall handed to the engine. It is not a claim about how real sheep move; what is proven exact is the conscience above.
